inconsistencies.issue: Two incompatible models of lateNotificationIndicator. D1 rules it derived on every read by a pure helper from journey.submittedAt — 'not stored', 'not a manifest obligation and not in SYSTEM_POPULATED', 'nothing is written at finalise', confirmation banner 'computed from journey.submittedAt' — and hedges that if c-030 admits Amend 'the records port must preserve the first-submission timestamp'. D5 admits Amend and rules the opposite: the flag is 'committed as a system value in fulfilment immediately before records.finalise when the journey is DRAFT' (a manifest obligation, so it must sit in SYSTEM_POPULATED per the boot-guard behaviour), because the backend and stub re-stamp submittedAt on every submission and a first-submission timestamp is 'new platform capability' (verified: stub/lifecycle/transition.js nulls submittedAt on amend and re-stamps on finalise). c-031 and c-030 both rewrite lateNotificationIndicator.input.derivation with contradictory text, and c-030's replace target is the pre-c-031 string ('computed once at submission ... stored with the record'), so whichever applies second either fails or overwrites the other. c-029's validationRaw ('lateness is computed at read from submittedAt') and c-024's rationale ('the stored late flag') sit on opposite sides.
inconsistencies.proposedFix: Make the D5 shape the single model, since Amend is in and no first-submission timestamp exists. Rewrite the D1 spec changes: c-035 notes/input.rendered and timing-window detail say the pure helper (clock, commodityType, arrivalDate) is called twice — with the request clock for the DRAFT CYA warning, and with the finalise clock in the declaration POST, whose result is committed as the system value before submitJourney only when status is DRAFT; confirmation, submitted CYA and the dashboard Late tag read the stored value and never recompute from submittedAt; keep lateNotificationIndicator in the manifest with system: true and listed in SYSTEM_POPULATED (boot-guard-dispatch-coverage requires it). Delete D1's 'records port must preserve the first submittedAt' contingency and c-029's 'computed at read from submittedAt'. Keep c-030's input.derivation as the canonical text and fold c-031's calendar-day rule into it rather than replacing the field twice. The mapper omission assertion stays (no typed backend field) — that is unaffected.

inconsistencies.issue: c-025 (D4) deletes the contactNumber and contactEmail obligations and the contact-details page. c-011 (D3) rules validation for both — a new email-shape pattern on contactEmail and a note on contactNumber — with specChanges targeting the deleted obligations, and its resolution sentence still says 'contactEmail gets a minimal shape check'; nfr-data-validation's adopted detail cites 'an email-shape pattern on contactEmail' and parks a telephone rule. c-034 (D6) keeps the page: 'contact-details runStep: 10 (was 11)' and its opening-run sequence ends '-> consignment-contact-select -> contact-details -> hub'. c-025 says the run 'ends at consignment-contact-select (runStep 10)' while c-034 renumbers that page to 9. Verified in journey-spec.json: contact-details exists at runStep 11 and both obligations exist.
inconsistencies.proposedFix: c-034 drops the contact-details runStep line and '-> contact-details' from its opening-run sequence (consignment-contact-select is runStep 9 and the last run step); c-025's 'runStep 10' reads 'runStep 9 after c-034's renumbering'. c-011 withdraws its contactEmail and contactNumber specChanges and its resolution reads 'contactEmail and contactNumber removed under c-025 — the address-book API validates phone and email at source; the only new factory is time'. nfr-data-validation's detail drops 'an email-shape pattern on contactEmail' and the parked telephone character-set rule. c-025's own c-011 fields edit stands.

inconsistencies.issue: provisionalCopy means two different things across dockets. D8 (c-038 dissent, spot-check-scheduling dissent) refuses the flag on declaration and confirmation because it is 'the invented-title flag' complementary to titleCy — which is what the brief says (RECONCILER-BRIEF.md:114-115; SPEC_RECONCILER.md:61, verified). D3 sets it on commodity-details, arrival-details and origin (titles verbatim animals), D4 on declaration (title verbatim) and on two obligations (consignmentNumber, countryOfOrigin), D6 on confirmation and hub (titles verbatim). Under D8's reading the D3/D4/D6 flags are wrong; under D3/D4/D6's reading D8's refusals are wrong.
inconsistencies.proposedFix: Pick one definition and record it in RECONCILER-BRIEF.md and SPEC_RECONCILER.md. Recommended: widen it — 'provisionalCopy=true on a page or obligation means it carries copy that is not verbatim animals and awaits the copy pass; the scope is stated in notes; titleCy stays wherever the title itself is verbatim' — then rewrite the c-038 and spot-check-scheduling dissent text to drop the narrow-flag argument (their other grounds stand). If the narrow reading is kept instead, strip the flag from every D3/D4/D6 change and carry the scope in notes.

standingRulingBreaches: conflict:c-038 (D8, decidedBy sam): builds a delegation-of-authority assertion in this phase — keeps the animals declaration sentence 'I can legally act on behalf of a third party in relation to the conditions of this declaration' verbatim. A declaration statement is a legal assertion the notifier signs, so this is delegation of authority (standing ruling 2), and it overrides c-028's explicit instruction that c-038 must not reinstate the clause. The retention is a panel choice (justified by standing ruling 5 at 'zero engine cost'), not a Sam ruling — drop the sentence.

behaviour:agent-acting-on-behalf (D8, decidedBy sam): same breach — 'The declaration keeps the one animals third-party sentence as copy (c-038)'; the park is right, the retained copy is not. Align with c-028's edit ('carries no third-party authority clause').

conflict:c-034 (D6, decidedBy panel): the declaration legal-limit note licenses statements asserting 'the notifier's standing as the professional operator or their authorised agent (c-028; NNS-UN-039)'. That is the GDS-judge sentence c-028 rejected under standing ruling 2 ('who is the notifier' and agent authority are out of phase); it also pre-empts c-038 by the back door. The item-level decidedBy 'panel' is defensible because the primary decision is the panel's, but each parked component should be recorded 'decidedBy sam (standing ruling 2)' in the detail, as c-025 does for name-of-person-making-entry and D7 does for nfr-secure-internal-login and equal-access-defra-policy-sg-fc.

Correctly attributed, for the record: conflict:c-039, conflict:c-040, behaviour:bulk-upload, behaviour:plant-operator-registration, behaviour:nfr-secure-internal-login, behaviour:equal-access-defra-policy-sg-fc (sam, rulings 2/3); behaviour:reference-number-prefix, behaviour:import-from-existing-documents, behaviour:document-uploads-out-of-scope, behaviour:outbox-and-gbnag-publishing-out-of-scope, behaviour:combined-ins-list-out-of-scope (panel under ruling 1 — no standing ruling names them). No ruling builds users, sign-in, operator registration or bulk upload.
summary: Coverage: all 83 docket items received exactly one ruling; no id is missing or duplicated. The only coverage blemish is that the ten D7 ids carry a 'behaviour:' prefix the other dockets do not use. Cross-docket consistency: six substantive contradictions need a decision — (1) lateNotificationIndicator is read-time-derived and unstored in D1 but stored as a system value at first finalise in D5, with c-031 and c-030 both rewriting the same input.derivation field (D5's shape should win because Amend is in and no first-submission timestamp exists; verified against stub/lifecycle/transition.js and the boot-guard SYSTEM_POPULATED rule); (2) D4 deletes contactNumber, contactEmail and the contact-details page while D3 rules validation on them and D6 keeps the page as run step 10 (D3/D6 conform to D4; run ends at consignment-contact-select as step 9); (3) the Balearic sentence is a page-side inset in D2 but an obligation-level hintByCategory with different copy in D3 (keep D2's inset); (4) countryOfOrigin is called same-as-animals in D3 while D3 itself changes its validation and D4 retags it variant-of-animals (tag variant once, with both divergences); (5) commodityType.valueHints is set to two different strings by c-031 and guidance-before-you-start, and D6's constants rule is not honoured by c-031/c-035 (single string reading the constants); (6) c-028 removes the declaration's third-party clause and forbids c-038 from reinstating it, c-038 reinstates it, and c-034 licenses a professional-operator/agent statement c-028 rejected (c-038/c-034 conform to c-028). Five vocabulary/convention drifts also need one answer each: provisionalCopy is the invented-title flag in D8 and the brief (verified) but an 'invented copy' flag in D3/D4/D6; parked behaviours are left open-question in D1/D6/D7/D8 but set 'parked' in D5, and D1's claim that the spec script rejects 'parked' is wrong (spec-set-behaviour-status.sh accepts it); c-026 writes a derived page gate as an authored-gate object where c-002 nulls it; c-032's 'four' Sam-gated chrome decisions become six after D7; and a handful of stale cross-references (reuse-previous-consignment's conditional on c-030, guidance-before-you-start treating c-001 as open and quoting the old arrivalStatus hint, spot-check-scheduling quoting the pre-c-006 destination hint, nfr-minimise-trader-effort's 'no optional obligation'). Standing rulings: three breaches of ruling 2, all the same clause — c-038 and D8's agent-acting-on-behalf keep an 'act on behalf of a third party' declaration sentence, and c-034 licenses a professional-operator/authorised-agent statement — plus attribution drift where four panel-marked items contain ruling-2 sub-parks (c-003, c-028, c-033, service-name-feedback-and-support). Nothing builds users, sign-in, operator registration or bulk upload; sam/panel attribution is otherwise correct.
